He began his career in the Australian state leagues before moving to the United States in 2019 to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's Gaels]]. He played five seasons for the Gaels and earned second-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] in 2022 and 2024. He played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) during the 2024–25 season, on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He was a member of the Thunder's 2025 [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]]-winning team. ==Early life and career== Ducas was born and raised in [[Geraldton]], [[Western Australia]],{{cite College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra College]]|access-date=2 September 2024}} ==College career== On 5 November 2019, Ducas made his debut for [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]], recording 3 points and 2 rebounds against [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite web|title=Saint Mary's Gaels vs Wisconsin Badgers - Boxscore|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401175202|website=ESPN.com|access-date=7 July 2024}} As a freshman, Ducas appeared in 33 games, starting in 11 games – which was more games as a true freshman than any Gael since [[Matthew Dellavedova]].{{cite web|title=Santa Mary's Gaels: Alex Ducas's Bio|url=https://smcgaels.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/alex-ducas/5554|website=SMCGaels.com|access-date=7 July 2024}} In his sophomore season, Ducas suffered an ankle injury, causing him to appear in only 14 games. Prior to his injury, Ducas averaged 11.3 points on 35.7% from three. He posted 10.3 points per game as a junior.{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Kroner|title=St. Mary’s forward Alex Ducas returning for a 5th season|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/st-mary-s-forward-alex-ducas-returning-5th-17891710.php|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=11 April 2023|access-date=16 July 2024}} As a senior, Ducas averaged 12.5 points per game shooting 41.4% from beyond the arc.{{cite news|first=Randall|last=Sweet|title=Why Two-Way Signee Alex Ducas Could be More Than a Summer League Star for OKC Thunder|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/draft-coverage/why-two-way-signee-alex-ducas-could-be-more-than-a-summer-league-star-for-okc-thunder-01j1mz0jfava|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 30, 2024|access-date=July 16, 2024}} In his final season with Saint Mary's, Ducas started every single game for the third consecutive season, shooting a career-best 43.8% from three, making 81 – which was the ninth most in team history and second most in the [[West Coast Conference|WCC]]. Against [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]], Ducas registered a season-high 23 points on 7 made threes.{{cite web|title=Saint Mary's Gaels vs Davidson Wildcats - Boxscore|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401597833|website=ESPN.com|access-date=7 July 2024}} With Saint Mary's, Ducas won the [[2024 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2024 WCC tournament]] and was named a second team All-WCC honoree for the second time.{{cite web|title=WCC Announces 2023-24 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2024/2/18/athlete-awards-wcc-announces-2023-24-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards.aspx|website=WCCSports.com|access-date=7 July 2024}} Ducas averaged 9.9 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. As a fifth year guard, Ducas finished his collegiate career playing in a program-record 150 games and finished second all-time in program history with 278 threes.{{cite web|title=MBB: Ducas Signs Two Way Deal with the Oklahoma City Thunder|url=https://smcgaels.com/news/2024/6/27/mens-basketball-mbb-ducas-sings-two-way-deal-with-the-oklahoma-city-thunder.aspx|website=SMCGaels.com|date=27 June 2024|access-date=7 July 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2024–2025)=== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]],{{cite web|last=Paddick|first=Matthew|url=https://www.geraldtonguardian.com.au/news/geraldton-guardian/geraldtons-alex-ducas-set-to-sign-with-oklahoma-city-thunder-in-nba-following-five-years-in-us-college-system-c-15174478|title=Geraldton's Alex Ducas set to sign with Oklahoma City Thunder in NBA following five years in US college system|work=[[Geraldton Guardian]]|date=28 June 2024|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240630130121/https://www.geraldtonguardian.com.au/news/geraldton-guardian/geraldtons-alex-ducas-set-to-sign-with-oklahoma-city-thunder-in-nba-following-five-years-in-us-college-system-c-15174478|archive-date=30 June 2024}} Ducas joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|title=Thunder Announces 2024 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/summer-league-roster-2024|website=NBA.com|date=7 July 2024|access-date=7 July 2024}} but did not play.{{cite web |title=Alex Ducas Player Profile, Oklahoma City Thunder - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Alex-Ducas/Summary/131564 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=28 July 2025 |language=en}} On 16 July 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Alex Ducas to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-ducas-240705|website=NBA.com|date=16 July 2024|access-date=16 July 2024}} He scored his first NBA points in January 2025 after a back injury sidelined him for nearly two months.{{cite news |last1=O'Donoghue |first1=Craig |title=Ducas on the board with first points in NBA |url=https://thewest.com.au/news/mid-west/geraldtons-alex-ducas-scores-first-nba-points-as-oklahoma-city-thunder-thump-washington-wizards-c-17381210 |access-date=15 January 2025 |work=The West Australian |date=15 January 2025 |language=en}} He featured in 21 NBA games during the regular season, averaging 1.7 points and 1.2 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Robinson |first1=Chris |title=Alex Ducas: Geraldton product becomes ninth Australian to earn NBA championship ring as Oklahoma City triumph |url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/sport/basketball/alex-ducas-geraldton-product-becomes-ninth-australian-to-earn-nba-championship-ring-as-oklahoma-city-triumph-c-19125342 |access-date=23 June 2025 |work=PerthNow |date=23 June 2025 |language=en}} He also played in six games for the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]] during the [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–25 season]].{{cite web |title=Alex Ducas G-League Stats |url=https://aws.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/d/ducasal01d.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=23 June 2025 |language=en}} Although Ducas did not play for the Thunder during their playoff run, he was part of the squad that won the NBA championship in the [[2025 NBA Finals]], making him the ninth Australian-born player to earn an NBA title. Ducas re-joined the Thunder for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]], playing one game in Salt Lake City. ===Brisbane Bullets (2025–2026)=== On 28 July 2025, Ducas signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]].{{cite news |title=Bullets sign NBA Champion |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bullets-sign-nba-champion-alex-ducas |access-date=28 July 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=28 July 2025 |language=en}} He averaged 8.5 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game across 30 appearances.{{Cite web|title=Balkan Botevgrad lands former NBA champion Alex Ducas|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/el-signing-geoff/|date=17 August 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=18 August 2026}} ===Balkan Botevgrad (2026–present)=== On 17 August 2026, Ducas signed with [[BC Balkan Botevgrad|Balkan Botevgrad]] of the Bulgarian [[National Basketball League (Bulgaria)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). ==National team career== Ducas played for [[Australia men's national under-19 basketball team|Australia]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web |title=Alexander Ducas (Australia) - Basketball Stats, Height, Age {{!}} FIBA Basketball |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/250101-alexander-ducas |website=www.fiba.basketball |access-date=24 October 2025 |language=en |date=24 October 2025}} Ducas debuted for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] at the [[2022 FIBA Asia Cup]]. He later played for the Boomers during the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 Asian Qualifiers]]. In October 2025, Ducas was named in the Boomers squad for the first window of the [[2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers]].{{cite news |title=Boomers confirmed for NZ double-header |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4388280/boomers-confirmed-for-nz-double-header |access-date=24 October 2025 |work=www.australia.basketball
